thread:
sarah.security: FYI CVE-2026-1457 just popped up in the base image layer we're using (buster-libc) — upstream released patch. We need an emergency rebuild + signed image rotation.
matt.eng-runtime: ack. can you paste the CVE link and affected packages? I want to check which models/runtimes are impacted.
sarah.security: https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2026-1457 — glibc locale parsing vuln. Affects libc < 2.33 on our base. Image manifest: `redwood/base:2024-09-12` includes `libc6 2.31`.
julia.sre: how severe is exploitability at runtime for inference traffic? remote code exec?
sarah.security: exploit allows crafted input leading to heap corruption in locale routines. RCE on attacker-controlled input possible in some configs. Risk: medium-high for any service that exposes locale parsing on attacker-controlled strings. Need patch.
oliver.devops: suggested plan: (1) downstream patch -> rebuild images with libc 2.34 (buster backports) (2) sign and push to prod registry, (3) tag and ramp via canary, (4) revoke old signed tags for critical clusters. Anyone see blockers?
matt.eng-runtime: +1. Questions: do we need to rotate KMS key used for cosign? Our signing key is in KMS keyring `projects/rw-prod/locations/global/keyRings/release/cryptoKeys/image-signer`.
sarah.security: we don't need to rotate the key unless it was compromised. But we need to ensure audit logs capture the signing operation and the new image push. Add additional audit entries for `roles/cloudkms.sign` and registry push.
carol.prodops: ok to add a short window of RBAC lock before pushing? i'd like deploys to prod paused until the canary passes. we can add a temporary deny for `serviceaccount:staging-deployer` to prod registry push.
julia.sre: propose a timeline: start rebuild now (10m), push to staging with canary at 10% for 30m, if good, ramp to 100% in 30m. We should also have rollback playbook ready.
ben.legal: looped in for compliance: notify audit team and keep all artifact signatures + SBOMs retained for 90 days. Also preserve CI logs.
matt.eng-runtime: commands I'll run for build/sign/push (copying for visibility):
```
# build
docker build -t gcr.io/redwood-releases/base:2026-06-18 --build-arg BASE=buster-backports .
# generate SBOM
syft packages gcr.io/redwood-releases/base:2026-06-18 -o cyclonedx > sbom-2026-06-18.xml
# sign with KMS-backed cosign
COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 cosign sign --kms "gcpkms://projects/rw-prod/locations/global/keyRings/release/cryptoKeys/image-signer" gcr.io/redwood-releases/base:2026-06-18
# push
docker push gcr.io/redwood-releases/base:2026-06-18
```
oliver.devops: add image attestation after signing and upload SBOM to our artifact store `gs://rw-artifacts/sbom/base/2026-06-18.xml` — also set object ACL to `private` and enable retention.
sarah.security: RBAC changes — i recommend creating a short-lived role binding to disallow `deploy` from prod CI while we rotate. Example kubectl patch for prod registry secret to limit `imagePullSecrets` updates:
```
kubectl -n prod patch rolebinding prod-deployer-binding -p '{"subjects": [{"kind": "ServiceAccount","name": "staging-deployer","namespace": "staging"}]}'
```
but we should be careful; maybe better to change a gateway flag to pause automated rollouts.
julia.sre: agree, we prefer toggling `rollout.controller.enabled=false` in the deployment config for 20m rather than messing with RBAC.
matt.eng-runtime: one more thing: runtime compatibility with glibc 2.34 — we need to run quick smoke tests for model startup and kv cache behavior. I'll run them in staging after the canary image is live.
carol.prodops: deploy-bot: please create the canary job + tag the run with `incident: CVE-2026-1457` so it's searchable.
deploy-bot: Canary job created: runs/canary-1913456789 — target 10% traffic, 30m.
oliver.devops: vuln triage note: mark internal tracker `SEC-1124` and link to GH PR that bumps base image: https://github.com/redwood-inference/base-images/pull/487
sarah.security: incident response checklist items:
- notify customers per SLA if PROD exploit signs appear
- preserve k8s audit logs from last 72h to `gs://rw-audit/tmp/SEC-1124/`
- collect container runtime logs from affected nodes
- rotate credentials if any suspicious pushes are detected
- open a postmortem if we see exploitation

matt.eng-runtime: running smoke tests now, will post results in 15m.
julia.sre: if smoke fails, we rollback to `redwood/base:2024-09-12` and block new deploys until patch fixed.
carol.prodops: thanks all — please add short notes to the incident channel and to the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/base-image-rotation
sarah.security: one more: file an internal memo for compliance with timestamps of sign/push and include SBOM and cosign signatures. Ben will confirm retention.
ben.legal: confirmed, retain artifacts 90 days and mark incident record. If customer notification needed we'll coordinate messaging.
matt.eng-runtime: smoke tests OK in staging (all 6 probes pass). Starting canary push.
carol.prodops: canary traffic at 10% now.
matt.eng-runtime: canary looks clean after 30m. No regressions in latency or errors.
julia.sre: rolling to 100% now. Monitoring on.
carol.prodops: rollout complete. old tag deprecated: `redwood/base:2024-09-12` -> marked EOL and set to non-pull in registrar.
sarah.security: closing incident in tracker SEC-1124. summarize actions and attach SBOM + cosign signature.
matt.eng-runtime: summary: patched libc -> rebuilt base -> signed w/ KMS -> canary -> full rollout. No evidence of exploit. Closing thread.
